title: Snowsports School Tuition and Add-On Charges: the Basis on Which Amounts Are Raised
content:
This page carries the Snowsports School basis for raising tuition and add-on charges against a household account, and marks those of its clauses that have been withdrawn.

## 1. Clauses withdrawn from this basis

The following clause is **no longer in force**: "The tuition raised for a booking is the product's block price where the product is sold as a block, and its session price multiplied by the number of sessions booked where it is sold session by session." It has been superseded by the current basis on which tuition is raised, and is carried here only so that no reader applies it.

The following clause is likewise **no longer in force**: "The season passholder reduction is taken first where the product carries one and the participant is shown on the collective's records as holding a pass in the active state, then the group reduction, and the result is rounded to the cent."

The following clause is likewise **no longer in force**: "Add-ons the household asks for are raised as their own entries at the product's add-on prices, one entry for each kind of add-on and each session date, and an add-on already included in the product is never raised as a charge."

## 2. Clauses in force

**2.1 State of the booking.** Tuition is raised only while the booking record stands in the asked-for, waiting, firm or under-way state. The state is read from the booking record itself, matched by the booking reference, before the tuition is raised; a booking that has reached the delivered, cancelled, missed or closed state is outside the clause.

**2.2 Deposits.** A product sold with a deposit raises the whole tuition at once and collects the deposit share of it at booking, with the balance falling due later; the deposit is not a separate price.

## 3. The state clause put as a table

| State of the booking record | Tuition may be raised |
| --- | --- |
| asked for | yes |
| waiting | yes |
| firm | yes |
| under way | yes |
| delivered | no |
| cancelled | no |
| missed | no |
| closed | no |

## 4. Reading of the deposit clause

A product sold at a deposit share below the whole price raises its tuition in one entry for the whole amount; the deposit share governs how much of that amount is collected at booking, and the rest falls due later. Nothing about the deposit changes the figure raised. The deposit shares, the session and block prices, the add-on prices and the named-instructor fee this basis speaks of are published product by product on the Snowsports School tariff.

superseded_clauses: The tuition raised for a booking is the product's block price where the product is sold as a block, and its session price multiplied by the number of sessions booked where it is sold session by session.

The season passholder reduction is taken first where the product carries one and the participant is shown on the collective's records as holding a pass in the active state, then the group reduction, and the result is rounded to the cent.

Add-ons the household asks for are raised as their own entries at the product's add-on prices, one entry for each kind of add-on and each session date, and an add-on already included in the product is never raised as a charge.
